I have updated r-cran-lobstr and r-cran-reticulate, plus r-cran-gstat and

going to attempt the simplest partial upgrade unless it is gets hints.

will try adding reciprocal Breaks statements between the two packages.

However, there is also a riscv64 regression tests failure related to NA
handling in r-cran-sparsevctrs, that blocks r-cran-vctrs migration in any case
because r-cran-sparsevctrs will always be re-tested when attempting to migrate
r-cran-vctrs.  We may need the help of the Release team to bypass it if we want
to speed up the process.

https://ci.debian.net/packages/r/r-cran-sparsevctrs/testing/riscv64/70697637/

Alternatively, we can also ask the Release team for their help on how to force
r-base in Testing directly by removing the old versions of the packages that it
breaks.

Have a nice day,

Charles

How would you define such a transition?

Usually, a .ben file has three regexes; one matching affected
packages, one matching 'bad' packages, and one matching 'good'
packages. e.g. a transition of libfoo might need rebuilds of all
packages with Build-Depends: libfoo-dev, 'bad' packages Depends:
libfoo4, and 'good' packages Depends: libfoo5, where 4 and 5 match the
SOVERSON of the library.

The regexes could also be on virtual packages, as is the case of
